title: Temurah 6
description: The Gemara tests Abaye and Rava on whether an act the Torah forbids takes effect once done, through Temple maintenance, robbery, collateral, pe’a and interest, then turns to the prohibitions against consecrating a blemished animal and the blemished scapegoat.
topics: 🏛️ Unblemished animals consecrated for Temple maintenance: “what he did is done”
🪵 Robbery, collateral and pe’a: why each case does not decide between Abaye and Rava
🍇 One who renounces ownership of his vineyard and harvests it at dawn
💰 Fixed interest and a hint of interest: Rabbi Elazar, Rabbi Yoḥanan and their verses
🧥 A cloak worth five given for four dinars of interest
🚫 Five prohibitions for one who consecrates a blemished animal for the altar
🐐 “Unto the Lord”: does it include or exclude the scapegoat?
🎲 The lottery of the goats: Ḥanan the Egyptian, Rabbi Shimon and Rava

a1.he: ״נְדָבָה תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתוֹ״ — זֶה קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת, וּתְנַן: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ תְּמִימִין לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה — מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה עָשׂוּי. תְּיוּבְתָּא דְרָבָא!

a2.he: אָמַר לָךְ [רָבָא]: מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁנִּתְרַבּוּ בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, נִתְרַבּוּ תְּמִימִין לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת.

a3.he: וַהֲרֵי גָּזֵל, דְּרַחֲמָנָא אָמַר ״לֹא תִגְזוֹל״, וּתְנַן: הַגּוֹזֵל עֵצִים וַעֲשָׂאָן כֵּלִים, צֶמֶר וַעֲשָׂאָן בְּגָדִים — מְשַׁלֵּם כִּשְׁעַת הַגְּזֵילָה, תְּיוּבְתָּא דְרָבָא!

a4.he: אָמַר לָךְ רָבָא: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאָמַר קְרָא ״אֲשֶׁר גָּזָל״ — כְּמָה שֶׁגָּזַל.

a5.he: וּלְאַבָּיֵי, הַאי ״אֲשֶׁר גָּזָל״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ: עַל גְּזֵילוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ, עַל גְּזֵילוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו אֵינוֹ מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ.

a6.he: וַהֲרֵי מַשְׁכּוֹן, דְּרַחֲמָנָא אָמַר: ״לֹא תָבֹא אֶל בֵּיתוֹ לַעֲבוֹט עֲבוֹטוֹ״, וּתְנַן: מַחֲזִיר אֶת הַכַּר בַּלַּיְלָה וְאֶת הַמַּחֲרֵישָׁה בַּיּוֹם — תְּיוּבְתָּא דְרָבָא!

a7.he: אָמַר לָךְ רָבָא: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאָמַר קְרָא ״הָשֵׁב תָּשִׁיב״.

a8.he: וּלְאַבָּיֵי, אִי לָאו דְּאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא ״הָשֵׁב תָּשִׁיב״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא אִיסּוּרָא עֲבַד, אִי בָּעֵי נַיהְדַּר וְאִי בָּעֵי לָא נַהְדַּר, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן. (חסר לישנא אחרינא)

a9.he: וַהֲרֵי פֵּאָה, דְּרַחֲמָנָא אָמַר: ״לֹא תְכַלֶּה פְּאַת שָׂדְךָ בְּקוּצְרֶךָ״, וּתְנַן: מִצְוַת פֵּאָה לְהַפְרִישׁ מִן הַקָּמָה, לֹא הִפְרִישׁ מִן הַקָּמָה — יַפְרִישׁ מִן הָעֳמָרִים, לֹא הִפְרִישׁ מִן הָעֳמָרִים — יַפְרִישׁ מִן הַכְּרִי עַד שֶׁלֹּא מֵירְחוֹ.

a10.he: מֵירְחוֹ — מְעַשְּׂרוֹ וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ; מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמְרוּ: אַף מַפְרִישׁ מִן הָעִיסָּה, תְּיוּבְתָּא דְאַבָּיֵי!

a11.he: אָמַר לָךְ אַבַּיֵּי: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאָמַר קְרָא ״תַּעֲזוֹב״, ״תַּעֲזוֹב״ יַתִּירָא.

a12.he: וְרָבָא אָמַר לָךְ: יֵשׁ לְךָ עֲזִיבָה אַחֶרֶת שֶׁכָּזוֹ, וְאֵיזוֹ? זֶה הַמַּפְקִיר כַּרְמוֹ.

a13.he: דְּתַנְיָא: הַמַּפְקִיר כַּרְמוֹ, וְהִשְׁכִּים לַשַּׁחַר וּבְצָרוֹ — חַיָּיב בְּפֶרֶט וְעוֹלֵלוֹת, בְּשִׁכְחָה וּבְפֵאָה, וּפָטוּר מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר.

a14.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּשַׁנִּינַן כֹּל הָנֵי שִׁינּוּיֵי, דְּאַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא בְּמַאי פְּלִיגִי?

a15.he: בְּרִבִּית קְצוּצָה קָמִיפַּלְגִי, וְכִדְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: רִבִּית קְצוּצָה יוֹצְאָה בְּדַיָּינִין,

b1.he: אֲבַק רִבִּית אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה בְּדַיָּינִין, וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ רִבִּית קְצוּצָה אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה בְּדַיָּינִין.

b2.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם בִּסְבָרָא פְּלִיגִי? הָתָם בִּקְרָאֵי פְּלִיגִי! דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן? אָמַר קְרָא: ״בַּנֶּשֶׁךְ נָתַן וְתַרְבִּית לָקַח וָחָי לֹא יִחְיֶה״, לְחַיִּים נִיתַּן וְלֹא לְהִישָּׁבוֹן.

b3.he: רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר מֵהָכָא: ״וְיָרֵאתָ מֵּאֱלֹהֶיךָ... אֲנִי ה׳״ — לְמוֹרָא נְתַתִּיו, וְלֹא לְהִישָּׁבוֹן.

b4.he: רָבָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא: ״הַתּוֹעֵבוֹת הָאֵל עָשָׂה מוֹת יוּמָת דָּמָיו בּוֹ יִהְיֶה״, ״וְהוֹלִיד בֵּן פָּרִיץ שׁוֹפֵךְ דָּם״ — הוּקְּשׁוּ מַלְוֵי רִבִּית לְשׁוֹפְכֵי דָמִים: מָה שׁוֹפְכֵי דָּמִים לֹא נִיתְּנוּ לְהִישָּׁבוֹן, אַף מַלְוֵי רִבִּית לֹא נִיתְּנוּ לְהִישָּׁבוֹן.

b5.he: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר? דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״וְחֵי אָחִיךָ עִמָּךְ״ — אַהְדַּר לֵיהּ, כִּי הֵיכִי דְּנֵיחֵי עִמָּךְ.

b6.he: וְאֶלָּא בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא? בְּשִׁינּוּי קוֹנֶה.

b7.he: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא, בְּהָנֵי שִׁינּוּיֵי דְּשַׁנִּינַן, בְּרִבִּית קְצוּצָה — לְאַבָּיֵי לָא מַהְדַּר רִבִּית, לְרָבָא מַהְדַּר רִבִּית.

b8.he: וְהָא אַבָּיֵי נָמֵי סָבַר מַפְּקִינַן רִיבִּית קְצוּצָה בְּדַיָּינִין! דְּאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָדֵין דְּמַסֵּיק בְּחַבְרֵיהּ אַרְבַּע זוּזֵי בְּרִיבִּיתָא, וִיהַביה לֵיהּ לְמַלְוֶה (בְּחָנוּתֵיהּ) [בְּגַוַּיְיהוּ] גְּלִימָא דְּשָׁוֵי חַמְשָׁא בְּאַרְבְּעָה — כִּי מַפְּקִינַן מִינֵּיהּ, אַרְבְּעָה מַפְּקִינַן מִינֵּיהּ, וְהַאי זוּזָא בְּמַתָּנָה הוּא דִּיהַב לֵיהּ. וְרָבָא אָמַר: חַמְשָׁא מַפְּקִינַן מִינֵּיהּ. מַאי טַעְמָא? כּוּלַּהּ בְּתוֹרַת רִיבִּיתָא קָאָתֵי לִידֵיהּ!

b9.he: אֶלָּא, כִּי קָא מִיפַּלְגִי אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא בְּשִׁינּוּי קוֹנֶה.

b10.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״כׇּל אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ מוּם לֹא תַקְרִיבוּ״, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר? אִם בְּ״לֹא תִשְׁחֲטוּ״ — הֲרֵי כְּבָר אָמוּר לְמַטָּה! אֶלָּא מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״בַּל תַּקְרִיבוּ״? — ״בַּל תַּקְדִּישׁוּ״. מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ עוֹבֵר מִשּׁוּם חֲמִשָּׁה שֵׁמוֹת.

b11.he: מִשּׁוּם ״בַּל תַּקְרִיבוּ״, ״בַּל תַּקְדִּישׁוּ״, ״בַּל תִּשְׁחֲטוּ״, וּמִשּׁוּם ״בַּל תִּזְרְקוּ״, וּמִשּׁוּם ״בַּל תַּקְטִירוּ כּוּלּוֹ״, וּמִשּׁוּם ״בַּל תַּקְטִירוּ מִקְצָתוֹ״. מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אָמְרוּ: אַף קַבָּלַת הַדָּם.

b12.he: אָמַר מָר: אִם ״בַּל תִּשְׁחֲטוּ״ — הֲרֵי אָמוּר לְמַטָּה. הֵיכָן אָמוּר? דְּתַנְיָא: ״עַוֶּרֶת אוֹ שָׁבוּר אוֹ חָרוּץ אוֹ יַבֶּלֶת לֹא תַקְרִיבוּ״ — מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר? אִם ״בַּל תַּקְדִּישׁוּ״ — הֲרֵי כְּבָר אָמוּר לְמַעְלָה, אֶלָּא מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״בַּל תַּקְרִיבוּ״? — ״בַּל תִּשְׁחֲטוּ״.

b13.he: ״וְאִשֶּׁה לֹא תִתְּנוּ מֵהֶם״ — אֵלּוּ אִשִּׁים, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא כּוּלָּן, מִקְצָתָן מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״מֵהֶם״.

b14.he: זְרִיקַת דָּמִים מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״, ״לַה׳״ — לְרַבּוֹת שָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ.

b15.he: וְ״לַה׳״ — לְרַבּוֹת הוּא? וְהָתַנְיָא: אִי ״קׇרְבָּן״ — שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי אַף קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת, שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ ״קׇרְבָּן״, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַנַּקְרֵב אֶת קׇרְבַּן ה׳״!

b16.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״וְאֶל פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וְגוֹ׳״ — הָרָאוּי לְפֶתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם שׁוֹחֲטֵי חוּץ, שֶׁאֵין רָאוּי לְפֶתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד אֵין חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם שׁוֹחֲטֵי חוּץ.

b17.he: אוֹצִיא אֲנִי אֶת אֵלּוּ, וְלֹא אוֹצִיא פָּרַת חַטָּאת וְשָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ, שֶׁהֵן רְאוּיִין לְפֶתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד — תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״לַה׳״, מִי שֶׁמְּיוּחָדִין לַה׳, יָצְאוּ אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין מְיוּחָדִין לַה׳.

b18.he: אָמַר רָבָא: הָתָם, מֵעִנְיָינָא דִּקְרָא, ״וְאֶל פֶּתַח״ — לְרַבּוֹת, ״לַה׳״ — לְהוֹצִיא; הָכָא, דְּ״אִשֶּׁה״ — לְהוֹצִיא, ״לַה׳״ — לְרַבּוֹת.

b19.he: טַעְמָא דִּכְתַב קְרָא ״לַה׳״ הוּא דְּלָא מַיְיתֵי שָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ, הָא לָא רַבִּי קְרָא ״לַה׳״ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא שָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ בַּעַל מוּם שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי. מִכְּדִי, אֵין הַגּוֹרָל קוֹבֵעַ אֶלָּא בְּדָבָר הָרָאוּי!

b20.he: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הָא מַנִּי? חָנָן הַמִּצְרִי הִיא, דְּאָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ דָּם בְּכוֹס — מֵבִיא חֲבֵירוֹ וּמְזַוֵּוג לוֹ.

b21.he: נְהִי דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְחָנָן הַמִּצְרִי, דְּלָא הָוֵי דִּיחוּי, דְּלָא צְרִיךְ הַגְרָלָה — מִי שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ? דִּילְמָא מַיְיתֵי וּמַגְרִיל!

b22.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן — מֵבִיא חֲבֵירוֹ בְּלֹא הַגְרָלָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.

b23.he: רָבָא אָמַר: לֹא נִצְרְכָא, כְּגוֹן שֶׁהוּמַם בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם וְחִילְּלוֹ עַל חֲבֵירוֹ.

messages.text: 6a

Continued from 5b: Abaye holds that an act the Torah forbids is effective once done; Rava holds that it is not. The Gemara is raising cases against Rava, and has just begun with one who consecrates unblemished animals for Temple maintenance, “with regard to which the Merciful One states:”

“Either a bull or a lamb that has anything too long or too short, that may you offer for a gift; but for a vow it shall not be accepted”. This verse teaches that only blemished animals may be consecrated for Temple maintenance.

verse.he: וְשׁוֹר וָשֶׂה שָׂרוּעַ וְקָלוּט נְדָבָה תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתוֹ וּלְנֵדֶר לֹא יֵרָצֶה׃
verse.en: You may, however, present as a freewill offering an ox or a sheep with a limb extended or contracted; but it will not be accepted for a vow.

notes.he: ואמרינן לקמן (תמורה דף ז:) אלו קדשי בדק הבית ואיכא למשמע אותו אתה מתפיס לבדק הבית ואי אתה מתפיס תמימין לבדק הבית:
notes.en: “That may you offer for a gift [nedava]”: and we say below (Temurah 7b) that this refers to items consecrated for Temple maintenance. And one can infer [from the word otó, “it”]: “it” you may assign to Temple maintenance, but you may not assign unblemished animals to Temple maintenance.

notes.he: אותו שרוע וקלוט בעלי מומין כדמפרש בבכורות אתה מקדיש לבדק הבית ולא תמימין למזבח ומאותו פסוק עצמו איתרבי נמי תמימה לבדק הבית בהיקישא דמהאי קרא נמי נדבה תעשה אותו ולנדר לא ירצה איתרבו בעלי מומין למזבח דכתי' ולנדר לא ירצה:
notes.en: “It”: [The printed edition’s note: It seems one should read: as it is written, “too long or too short… that may you offer for a gift,” and these are blemished animals, as explained in Bekhorot; and we expound: “it” you may consecrate, but you may not consecrate unblemished animals for Temple maintenance. End of the comment.] Too long or too short are blemished animals, as explained in Bekhorot: those you consecrate for Temple maintenance, and not unblemished ones [which are] for the altar. [The printed edition’s note: One should read: from this verse, “that may you offer for a gift,” and blemished animals were included for the altar, as it is written “but for a vow it shall not be accepted,” unblemished animals were also included for Temple maintenance. This belongs to the next comment.] And from that same verse unblemished animals were also included for Temple maintenance, through the juxtaposition: for from this verse too, “that may you offer for a gift… but for a vow it shall not be accepted,” blemished animals were included for the altar, as it is written “but for a vow it shall not be accepted.”

messages.text: With regard to one who consecrates unblemished animals for Temple maintenance, even though he has transgressed a prohibition, what he did is done.

notes.he: כדדרשינן לקמן וידבר ה' אל משה לאמר לא אמור:
notes.en: With a prohibition: as we expound below: “And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying [lemor]” — [read it as] lo emor, “do not say” [that is, do not declare them consecrated].

messages.text: This is apparently a conclusive refutation of the opinion of Rava.

Rava could say to you: From the same place that it was derived earlier that blemished animals are included, i.e., that their consecration for sacrifice on the altar is effective after the fact, it is likewise derived that unblemished animals are included, that their consecration for Temple maintenance is effective. But in general, transgressions are not effective.

notes.he: דקדשי בדיעבד:
notes.en: From the place that blemished animals are included for the altar: that they become consecrated after the fact.

notes.he: דהא בההוא קרא כתיב ולנדר לא ירצה ואמרינן לקמן (תמורה דף ז:) אלו קדשי מזבח וכתיב לא ירצה דמשמע רצויי לא מרצו הא מקדש קדשי ואיתקוש תמימין לבדק הבית לבעלי מומין למזבח דהא מחד קרא נפקי לאיסורא דלא מקדיש הלכך איתקוש נמי לענין מה שעשה עשוי:
notes.en: Are included etc.: for in that very verse it is written, “But for a vow it shall not be accepted,” and we say below (Temurah 7b) that this refers to items consecrated for the altar. And it is written “it shall not be accepted,” implying that they do not effect acceptance, but if one consecrates them, they are consecrated. And unblemished animals for Temple maintenance are juxtaposed to blemished animals for the altar, since both come from one verse for the prohibition that one may not consecrate [them]. Therefore they are juxtaposed also with regard to “what he did is done.”

notes.he: אמר לך רבא שאני הכא דמהיכ' דאיתרבו בעלי מומין למזבח דכתיב ולנדר לא ירצה ארצוי הוא דלא מרצו ליקרב הא מקדש קדשי [איתרבו נמי תמימין לבה"ב] ואיתקש תמימין לבדק הבית לבעלי מומין למזבח מה בעלי מומין למזבח אמרינן אע"פ שהוא בלא תעשה מה שעשה עשוי אף תמימין לבדק הבית אע"פ שבלא תעשה מה שעשה עשוי:
notes.en: Rava could say to you: it is different here. For from the place that blemished animals were included for the altar, as it is written, “but for a vow it shall not be accepted” — it is effecting acceptance, being sacrificed, that they do not do, but if one consecrates them they are consecrated — [unblemished animals were also included for Temple maintenance]. And unblemished animals for Temple maintenance are juxtaposed to blemished animals for the altar: just as with blemished animals for the altar we say that even though it is [done] with a prohibition, what he did is done, so too with unblemished animals for Temple maintenance, even though it is with a prohibition, what he did is done.

messages.text: But there is the case of robbery, with regard to which the Merciful One states: “You shall not oppress your neighbor, and you shall not rob him”.

verse.he: לֹא־תַעֲשֹׁק אֶת־רֵעֲךָ וְלֹא תִגְזֹל לֹא־תָלִין פְּעֻלַּת שָׂכִיר אִתְּךָ עַד־בֹּקֶר׃
verse.en: You shall not defraud your fellow. You shall not commit robbery. The wages of a laborer shall not remain with you until morning.

messages.text: One who robs another of wood and fashions it into vessels, or one who robs another of wool and fashions it into garments, pays the victim according to the value of the goods at the time of the robbery,

notes.he: צמר ועצים בעלמא אבל הכלים והבגדים קנה בשינוי אלמא מהני:
notes.en: According to the time of the robbery: [the value of] plain wool and wood; but the vessels and the garments he acquired through the change. Evidently [the transgression] is effective.

notes.he: ולא כמו שהן עכשו מדאינו משלם כמעכשו אלא כשעת הגזילה אלמא מהני:
notes.en: He pays according to the time of the robbery: and not as they are now. Since he does not pay as they are now but according to the time of the robbery, evidently it is effective.

messages.text: But he need not return the vessels or garments, since by changing the stolen items he acquired them. If he can acquire the stolen item, this is apparently a conclusive refutation of the opinion of Rava.

notes.he: דשינוי קנה אלמא מהני ותיובתא דרבא:
notes.en: He pays according to the time of the robbery: for a change acquires; evidently it is effective, and it is a refutation of Rava.

messages.text: Rava could say to you: It is different there, as the verse states: “He shall restore the stolen item that he took by robbery”. This teaches that he must return the original item only if it is still like that which he took by robbery and has not been altered. But in general, transgressions are not effective.

verse.he: וְהָיָה כִּי־יֶחֱטָא וְאָשֵׁם וְהֵשִׁיב אֶת־הַגְּזֵלָה אֲשֶׁר גָּזָל אוֹ אֶת־הָעֹשֶׁק אֲשֶׁר עָשָׁק אוֹ אֶת־הַפִּקָּדוֹן אֲשֶׁר הׇפְקַד אִתּוֹ אוֹ אֶת־הָאֲבֵדָה אֲשֶׁר מָצָא׃
verse.en: when they have thus sinned and, realizing their guilt, would restore either that which was gotten through robbery or fraud, or the entrusted deposit, or the lost thing that was found,

notes.he: יחזיר:
notes.en: “That he took by robbery”: [he returns it only if it is] like what he robbed.

messages.text: And according to the opinion of Abaye, this phrase: “That he took by robbery,” is necessary to teach that one who takes a false oath denying he robbed another, who must then pay an additional fifth of the value of the stolen item when he returns it, need add a fifth only for denying his own act of robbery, but for denying his deceased father’s act of robbery when sued by the victim as the robber’s heir, he need not add an additional fifth.

notes.he: להכי לא איצטריך דאנא ידענא דמהני אלא להך דרשא דהאי אשר גזל כתיב גבי שבועה שנשבע לשקר וכתיב (ויקרא ה) יוסיף חומש וקמ"ל דעל גזילו מוסיף חומש אם נשבע לשקר והודה:
notes.en: And Abaye: [holds that the verse] is not needed for this, since I already know that [a transgression] is effective; rather, it is for this exposition. This “that he took by robbery” is written in connection with an oath that he swore falsely, and it is written (Leviticus 5) “he shall add a fifth.” It teaches us that for his own robbery he adds a fifth, if he swore falsely and then admitted.

notes.dh: ואינו מוסיף חומש על גזל אביו
notes.he: אפילו נשבע עליו לשקר:
notes.en: But he does not add a fifth for his father’s robbery: even if he swore falsely about it.

notes.he: להכי אתא האי אשר גזל דעל גזילו מוסיף חומש ולא על מה שגזל אביו:
notes.en: This “that he took by robbery” comes for this: that for his own robbery he adds a fifth, and not for what his father robbed.

messages.text: But there is the case of collateral, with regard to which the Merciful One states: “When you lend your neighbor any manner of loan, you shall not go into his house to fetch his pledge”, teaching that a creditor may not seize collateral if the debtor delays payment.

verse.he: כִּי־תַשֶּׁה בְרֵעֲךָ מַשַּׁאת מְאוּמָה לֹא־תָבֹא אֶל־בֵּיתוֹ לַעֲבֹט עֲבֹטוֹ׃
verse.en: When you make a loan of any sort to your compatriot, you must not enter the house to seize the pledge.

messages.text: If the creditor nevertheless seized two items as collateral, he returns a mattress by night, as the debtor requires it for sleeping, and a plow, which is needed for his daytime work, by day.

notes.he: וגבי ממשכנין בעל כרחו קתני לה בבבא מציעא בפ' המקבל (בבא מציעא דף קיג.). אלמא מהני וקני למשכון יום דהיינו מחרישה קני בלילה וכסות לילה קני מלוה ביום אלמא מהני:
notes.en: He returns the mattress at night etc.: this is taught in Bava Metzia, in chapter HaMekabel (Bava Metzia 113a), with regard to one who takes collateral against the debtor’s will. Evidently it is effective, and he acquires the collateral: an item for the day, that is, the plow, the creditor acquires at night, and a covering for the night the creditor acquires by day. Evidently it is effective.

notes.he: והרי משכון כו' [אלמא מדלא מחזיר כר ביום אלא בלילה ולא מחרישה אלא ביום] ש"מ דאי עביד מהני וקנייה למשכון דלא מהדר אלא [כר] בלילה וביום הדר שקיל ליה:
notes.en: But there is collateral etc.: [evidently, since he returns the mattress not by day but only at night, and the plow only by day,] learn from it that if one did it, it is effective, and he acquired it as collateral, for he returns [the mattress] only at night, and by day he goes back and takes it.

messages.text: The creditor may keep possession of seized collateral when it is not being used, which is apparently a conclusive refutation of the opinion of Rava.

notes.dh: מחזיר את הכר בלילה ואת המחרישה ביום ותיובתא דרבא
notes.he: דאי לא מהני לא היה תפיסתו תפיסה והיה לו להחזירם לבעלים מכל וכל ואם תאמר מנלן דהא מתניתין במשכנו שלא ברשות איירי דלמא במשכנו שליח בית דין קאמר דמחזיר הכר בלילה והמחרישה ביום דלא עבר אבל היכא דעבר אימא לך דלא מהני וי"ל דהך משנה מיתניא בפרק המקבל (ב"מ דף קיג.) גבי משכנו שלא ברשות דתני לעיל מיניה המלוה חבירו לא ימשכנו אלא בבית דין ולא יכנס לביתו ליטול משכונו שנאמר בחוץ תעמוד היו לו שני כלים נוטל אחד ומניח אחד מחזיר את הכר בלילה ואת המחרישה ביום אלמא אשלא ברשות קאי:
notes.en: He returns the mattress at night and the plow by day, and it is a refutation of Rava: for if it were not effective, his seizure would not be a valid seizure, and he would have to return them to the owners entirely. And if you say: from where do we know [that the mishna speaks of one who transgressed]? Perhaps it speaks of one who took collateral with permission, that is, the court’s agent took the collateral, and of him it says that he returns the mattress at night and the plow by day, since he did not transgress; but where he transgressed, I would say that it is not effective. One can say that this mishna is taught in chapter HaMekabel (Bava Metzia 113a) with regard to one who took collateral without permission, for just before it, it teaches: One who lends to another may take collateral from him only through the court, and he may not enter his house to take his collateral, as it is stated: “You shall stand outside.” If he had two items, he takes one and leaves one; he returns the mattress at night and the plow by day. Evidently it refers to [collateral taken] without permission.

messages.text: Rava could say to you: It is different there, as the verse states: “And if he be a poor man, you shall not sleep with his pledge; you shall restore [hashev tashiv] to him the pledge”. The repetition of the verb teaches that the creditor must return the collateral many times, e.g., he must return a plow each morning and take it back each night, and return a mattress each night and take it back each morning, but he does not have to return the collateral permanently. But in general, transgressions are not effective.

verse.he: וְאִם־אִישׁ עָנִי הוּא לֹא תִשְׁכַּב בַּעֲבֹטוֹ׃ הָשֵׁב תָּשִׁיב לוֹ אֶת־הַעֲבוֹט כְּבוֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְשָׁכַב בְּשַׂלְמָתוֹ וּבֵרְכֶךָּ וּלְךָ תִּהְיֶה צְדָקָה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃ {ס}
verse.en: And if they are needy, you shall not go to sleep in their pledge; you must return the pledge at sundown, that they may sleep in their cloth and bless you; and it will be to your merit before the ETERNAL your God.

notes.dh: שאני התם דכתיב השב תשיבנו לו
notes.he: מריבויא דקרא נפקא לן דמחזיר כמה פעמים ולא משכחת לה אלא הכי דמחזיר כלי יום ביום וכלי לילה בלילה ומהכא נפקא דקני. ולאביי ריבויא דקרא לא משמע ליה והשב תשיבנו איצטריך דאי לא כתיב ביה הוה אמינא איבעי ניהדר איבעי לא ניהדר:
notes.en: It is different there, as it is written: “You shall restore [hashev teshivenu] to him”: from the amplification of the verse we derive that he returns it many times, and that can only be found in this way: he returns an item for the day by day and an item for the night at night. And from here we derive that he acquires [it]. And for Abaye, the amplification of the verse does not imply this, and hashev teshivenu is needed, since if it were not written I would say: if he wants, he returns it, and if he wants, he does not return it.

notes.dh: ה"ג ל"א אמר לך רבא שאני התם דכתיב עד בא השמש תשיבנו
notes.he: ודרשינן ליה בהמקבל הכי כל היום עד שיבא השמש תשיבנו ללוה ובבוא השמש תקחנו ממנו מכאן לכסות יום שניתנה ליחבל בלילה וכתיב קרא אחרינא השב תשיבנו כבוא השמש מכאן לכסות לילה שניתנה ליחבל ביום ומהכא נפקא לן דמהני. ואביי אמר לך לאו לאשמועינן דמהני אלא חד לכסות יום שיחזירנו ביום וחד לכסות לילה שחייב להחזירו בלילה וצריכי. והאי וצריכי לא איתפרש לן ונראה לי דהכי הוא דאי אשמעינן לכסות יום כגון מחרישה משום דחיותיה הוא אבל כסות לילה אימא לא ואי כתיב כסות לילה משום דמצטער אבל כסות יום אימא לא:
notes.en: This is the version we read: Another version: Rava could say to you: It is different there, as it is written, “Until the sun goes down you shall restore it.” And we expound it in [chapter] HaMekabel thus: all day, until the sun sets, you shall restore it to the borrower, and when the sun sets you shall take it from him. From here [we learn] about a garment for the day, that it is given to be taken as collateral at night. And another verse is written: “You shall restore the pledge when the sun goes down” — from here [we learn] about a garment for the night, that it is given to be taken as collateral by day. And from here we derive that it is effective. And Abaye could say to you: [these verses come] not to teach us that it is effective, but rather one for a garment for the day, that he must return it by day, and one for a garment for the night, that he is obligated to return it at night; and both are necessary. And this “both are necessary” was not explained to us. It seems to me that it is thus: had it taught us about an item for the day, such as a plow, [I would say that is] because it is his livelihood, but a covering for the night, I would say not; and had it written a covering for the night, [I would say that is] because he suffers [without it], but a covering for the day, I would say not.

notes.dh: שאני התם דאמר קרא השב תשיב
notes.he: וא"ת הא דאמר פרק אלו מציאות (ב"מ דף לא:) השב תשיב אין לי [אלא] שמשכנו ברשות שלא ברשות מנין ת"ל השב תשיב מכל מקום משמע דאי לאו השב תשיב ה"א דמשכנו שלא ברשות אינו צריך השבה והכא אמר לרבא דאי לאו השב תשיב ה"א דלא מהני תפיסתו והיה צריך להחזיר מכל וכל וצריך לפרש לרבא הכי אין לי אלא שמשכנו ברשות דמחזיר ונוטלה אבל משכנו שלא ברשות מנין דחוזר ונוטלה דמהניא תפיסתו ת"ל השב תשיב מכל מקום ולאביי ה"פ אין לי אלא דצריך להחזיר כלל אלא שמשכנו ברשות משכנו שלא ברשות מנין דצריך להחזיר לו כלל כיון דעביד מהני ולא מהדר ת"ל השב תשיב מ"מ והכי נמי קאמר הכא דלאביי אי לאו דאמר רחמנא השב תשיב ה"א איסורא עבד ואי בעי מהדר ואי בעי לא מהדר קמ"ל וקשה מההיא דסוף פ' המקבל (ב"מ דף קטז.) דההוא גברא דחבל סכינא דאשכבתא מחבריה אתא לקמיה דאביי א"ל זיל אהדר משום דברים שעושין בהן אוכל נפש וכיון דאית ליה לאביי דאי עבד מהני אמאי קא"ל זיל אהדר וי"ל דמיירי שלא נתכוין ההוא גברא לעבור ומהאי טעמא נמי ניחא קושיא אחרת דתנן פ' המקבל (בבא מציעא קטו.) חבל ריחיים ורכב לוקה שתים וקשה כיון דאית ליה לאביי דאית ליה תקנה בחזרה כדאמר גבי סכינא דאשכבתא זיל אהדר א"כ אמאי לקי לאו הניתק לעשה הוא ולפי הא דפירשתי ניחא דהא דאמר אביי זיל אהדר מיירי בשלא נתכוין לעבור והא דתנן דלקי במתכוין לעבור ויש מתרצים דהא דאמר דלקי מיירי בשנאבד דאין בידו להחזיר ולא נהירא שהרי בפרק בתרא דמכות (דף טז:) משמע דהיכא דגברא בר תשלומין הוא לא מהני ביטול:
notes.en: In brief: Tosafot ask from Bava Metzia 31b, where “hashev tashiv” is expounded to include collateral taken without permission. That implies that without the verse, such collateral would not need to be returned at all, whereas here, for Rava, without the verse the seizure would be void and returned entirely. They answer that for Rava the baraita there means: from where do we know that he returns it and takes it back, i.e., that the seizure takes effect? And for Abaye it means: from where do we know that he must return it at all, since the act was effective? That fits our Gemara, which says that for Abaye, without the verse he might return it or not as he wished. They then ask from the end of chapter HaMekabel (Bava Metzia 116a), where Abaye told a man who had taken a knife (sakina de’ashkavta) as collateral, “Go return it,” since it is among the items used to prepare food: if for Abaye the act is effective, why return it? They answer that the man there did not intend to transgress. This also settles the mishna in Bava Metzia 115a that one who takes a mill and an upper millstone as collateral receives two sets of lashes, although for Abaye the prohibition can be remedied by returning the item: the lashes are where he intended to transgress. Others answer that the lashes are where the item was lost and cannot be returned; Tosafot reject this, since the last chapter of Makkot (16b) implies that where the man is able to pay, the nullification does not help. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: דבפירוש אשכחן דקני דמ[ד]איצטריך למיכתב השב תשיב ש"מ משום דקני למשכון. ל"א כיון דכתיב עד בא השמש כמו עד שנת היובל מזריחת השמש עד בא השמש תשיבנו לו ולא קודם מכלל דקני משכון דיום [מחרישה] בלילה ומדכתיב השב תשיב לו [את העבוט] כבוא השמש [דהיינו לשקיעה] ולא קודם מכלל דקני משכון דלילה [הכר] ביום דכל היום הכר הוא של מלוה עד שקיעה (שקיעת החמה):
notes.en: Rava could say to you: it is different there: for there we find explicitly that he acquires; since it was necessary to write “hashev tashiv,” learn from it that this is because he acquires the collateral. Another version: since it is written “until the sun goes down” — like “until the Jubilee year” — from sunrise until the sun goes down you shall return it to him, and not before; by implication, he acquires collateral for the day [the plow] at night. And since it is written, “You shall restore [the pledge] to him when the sun goes down” [that is, at sunset] and not before, by implication he acquires collateral for the night [the mattress] by day, for all day the mattress belongs to the creditor until sunset.

messages.text: And according to the opinion of Abaye, that transgressions are generally effective, the repetition of the verb may be explained as follows: If the Merciful One had not stated: “Hashev tashiv,” I would say that a creditor who seizes collateral from the home of the debtor has performed a prohibition, but having done so, if he desires, he may return the collateral, and if he desires, he may not return it. The verse therefore teaches us that he must return the items the debtor needs.

notes.dh: ואביי קסבר לא אתו אלא חד לכסות יום וחד לכסות לילה
notes.he: וצריך למילף דתרווייהו בעי מהדר ליה:
notes.en: And Abaye holds: they come only, one for a covering for the day and one for a covering for the night, and it is necessary to learn that for both he must return it to him.

messages.text: The printed Aramaic marks an “alternative version” (lishna aḥarina) as missing here. Rashi records one, in which the proof turns on the verses about returning the pledge by sunset (his second note on Rava’s answer above).

But there is the case of produce in the corner of the field, which is given to the poor [pe’a], with regard to which the Merciful One stated: “And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not wholly reap the corner of your field”, but one must leave a corner of the field for the poor.

verse.he: וּבְקֻצְרְכֶם אֶת־קְצִיר אַרְצְכֶם לֹא־תְכַלֶּה פְּאַת שָׂדְךָ בְּקֻצְרֶךָ וְלֶקֶט קְצִירְךָ לֹא תְלַקֵּט לֶעָנִי וְלַגֵּר תַּעֲזֹב אֹתָם אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃ {פ}
verse.en: And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not reap all the way to the edges of your field, or gather the gleanings of your harvest; you shall leave them for the poor and the stranger: I the ETERNAL am your God.

messages.text: The optimal way to fulfill the mitzva of pe’a is for the owner to separate it from the standing grain, i.e., grain that has not been harvested. If he did not separate it from the standing grain, he separates it from the sheaves of grain that have already been harvested. If he did not separate it from the sheaves, he separates it from the pile of grain, as long as he has not yet smoothed the pile.

notes.he: דאיקבע למעשר ולתרומה:
notes.en: He smoothed it [meiraḥo]: it has become fixed [as obligated] for tithe and for teruma.

messages.text: Once he smooths the pile of grain, it becomes obligated in tithes. Therefore, he must first tithe the grain and then give a portion of the produce to the poor as pe’a, so that the poor need not tithe what they receive.

notes.he: תחילה ואח"כ נותן (לה) פאה:
notes.en: He tithes: first, and afterward he gives the pe’a.

notes.he: ששיוה פני הכרי ונגמר מלאכתו למעשר אסור באכילה לכל אדם עד שיעשר הילכך מעשר ואח"כ נותן לו פאה:
notes.en: He smoothed it [meraḥo]: he leveled the surface of the pile, and its work was completed with respect to tithe; it is forbidden for anyone to eat until he tithes. Therefore he tithes, and afterward gives him pe’a.

messages.text: If he did not separate pe’a during any of these stages, and he milled the grain and kneaded it into dough, he separates pe’a even from the dough and gives it to the poor.

notes.he: ואין שינוי שם קונה:
notes.en: He separates even from the dough: and a change of name does not acquire [here].

notes.he: עד שלא הורמה חלתה ולכן מאחר שנתחייבה בחלה מפריש [חלתה ונותן פאה]:
notes.en: He separates even from the dough: before its ḥalla was taken. And therefore, once it has become obligated in ḥalla, he separates [its ḥalla and gives pe’a].

messages.text: Even if the owner harvested the grain, the pe’a is still not considered his, which is apparently a conclusive refutation of the opinion of Abaye.

notes.he: דאמר מהני דהא הכא לא מהני:
notes.en: A conclusive refutation of Abaye: who said [a transgression] is effective, for here it is not effective.

notes.he: דאלמא לא מהני אלא חייב ליתן מכל מקום:
notes.en: A refutation of Abaye: for evidently it is not effective; rather, he is obligated to give in any case.

messages.text: Abaye could say to you: It is different there, as the verse states: “You shall leave them for the poor and for the stranger” (Leviticus 19:10), and subsequently, it again states: “You shall leave them for the poor and for the stranger” (Leviticus 23:22). The superfluous phrase teaches that the owner must give pe’a in any event, even if he harvests the grain and kneads it into dough. But in general, transgressions are effective.

verse.he: וְכַרְמְךָ לֹא תְעוֹלֵל וּפֶרֶט כַּרְמְךָ לֹא תְלַקֵּט לֶעָנִי וְלַגֵּר תַּעֲזֹב אֹתָם אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃
verse.en: You shall not pick your vineyard bare, or gather the fallen fruit of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the poor and the stranger: I the ETERNAL am your God.

notes.he: תרי זימני כתיב לעני ולגר תעזוב אותם חד בקדושים תהיו וחד באמור אל הכהנים לאשמועינן מקרא דתעזוב יתירא דאע"ג דאישתני בידו לא קנייה:
notes.en: “You shall leave,” “you shall leave”: “You shall leave them for the poor and for the stranger” is written twice, once in [the portion of] Kedoshim Tihyu and once in Emor el HaKohanim, to teach us from the superfluous “you shall leave” that even though it changed in his hand, he did not acquire it.

notes.dh: אמר אביי שאני התם דאמר קרא (עזב) תעזוב ורבא אמר לך כו'
notes.he: וא"ת הכא משמע דלאביי איצטריך תעזוב יתירא ולרבא לא איצטריך ובריש הגוזל עצים (ב"ק דף צד.) משמע איפכא דאביי מוכח מהך מילתא דרבי ישמעאל דשינוי במקומו עומד ורבא דחי ליה ואמר שאני הכא דכתיב תעזוב יתירא וי"ל דהכא אליבא דת"ק איירי דלאביי דאמר אי עביד מהני אי לא כתיב תעזוב יתירא לא היה צריך להפריש פאה מיד שעבר אלא תכלה מיהו לת"ק אי אשתני בידו ועשה ממנו עיסה קנאה בשינוי ואינו צריך להפריש פאה מכאן ואילך אבל ר' ישמעאל דאמר יפריש מן העיסה אית ליה דשינוי במקומו עומד דאי הוה ס"ל בעלמא דשינוי קונה לא היה מפריש מן העיסה ואע"ג דכתיב תעזוב יתירא איצטריך שפיר להיכא דלא אישתני אע"ג דבעלמא אי עביד מהני הכא לא מהני משום דכתיב תעזוב יתירא אבל רבא דאית ליה דאי עבד לא מהני משום הכי קאמר ת"ק דצריך להפריש פאה אע"ג דעבר אלא תכלה ואין צריך תעזוב יתירא לת"ק להכי מיהו היכא דאישתני פטור דשינוי קונה ור' ישמעאל סבר דבעלמא שינוי קונה אבל הכא לא קנה משום דכתיב תעזוב יתירא:
notes.en: In brief: Tosafot ask that here Abaye needs the extra “you shall leave” and Rava does not, while at the start of HaGozel Etzim (Bava Kamma 94a) it is the reverse: Abaye proves from this statement of Rabbi Yishmael that a change does not acquire, and Rava rejects the proof because the extra “you shall leave” is written. They answer that our Gemara speaks according to the first tanna. For Abaye, without the extra verse one who transgressed “you shall not wholly reap” would not have to separate pe’a at all; but according to the first tanna, once the grain changed in his hand into dough he acquired it through the change and need not separate pe’a from then on. Rabbi Yishmael, who has him separate even from the dough, holds that a change does not acquire, and the extra verse is still needed for grain that has not changed: although in general a transgression is effective, here it is not. For Rava, who holds that a transgression is not effective, the first tanna needs no extra verse to require pe’a after the transgression, and once the grain changed he is exempt, since a change acquires; and Rabbi Yishmael holds that a change acquires in general but not here, because of the extra “you shall leave.” Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: דהוה יכול למימר לעני ולגר עזב מאי תעזב ריבה מ"מ:
notes.en: “You shall leave,” “you shall leave” [azov ta’azov]: for it could have said “leave [azov] for the poor and for the stranger”; why “you shall leave [ta’azov]”? It includes: in any case.

messages.text: And Rava, who maintains that in general transgressions are not effective, could say to you that the extra verse teaches that there is another type of leaving over one’s grain that is like this. And what is that? It is the case of one who renounces ownership of his vineyard.

If one renounced ownership of his vineyard, thereby exempting it from tithes and gifts to the poor, and he rose early in the morning, retook possession of it, and harvested it, he is still obligated in the mitzva of individual fallen grapes left for the poor [peret], and in the mitzva of incompletely formed clusters of grapes left for the poor [olelot], and in the mitzva of forgotten clusters of grapes left for the poor, and in the mitzva of pe’a, but he remains exempt from the mitzva to tithe his produce.

notes.he: ואע"ג דהפקר פטור מכל אלו הפקר כי האי חייב דנפקא לן מתעזוב יתירא דבכולהו כתיב תעזוב יתירא:
notes.en: He is obligated in peret and olelot etc.: even though ownerless property is exempt from all of these, ownerless property like this is obligated. We derive this from the superfluous “you shall leave,” since with all of them the superfluous “you shall leave” is written.

notes.he: דבמעשר לא כתיב תעזוב יתירא ולרבויי האי הפקר אתא תעזוב ולא לרבויי שינוי דהא בעלמא נמי לא מהני:
notes.en: And exempt from tithe: for with tithe the superfluous “you shall leave” is not written. And the [extra] “you shall leave” comes to include this ownerless property, and not to include a change, for in general too [according to Rava, a transgression] is not effective.

notes.dh: המפקיר כרמו והשכים לבקר ובצרו חייב בפרט ובעוללות ובשכחה ופאה
notes.he: פירש"י אע"ג דהפקר פטור מכל אלו הפקר כי האי חייב ונפקא לן מתעזוב יתירא דבכולהו כתיב תעזוב יתירא ואור"י דהחיוב תלוי היכא דזכה בגוף השדה אבל היכא דלא זכה רק בפירות פטור מכולהו:
notes.en: One who renounced ownership of his vineyard, and rose early in the morning and harvested it, is obligated in peret, olelot, forgotten clusters and pe’a: Rashi explained: even though ownerless property is exempt from all of these, ownerless property like this is obligated, and we derive it from the superfluous “you shall leave,” since with all of them the superfluous “you shall leave” is written. And the Ri says that the obligation applies where he acquired the field itself; but where he acquired only the fruit, he is exempt from all of them.

notes.he: דכל הני כתיב בהו תעזוב דריבה אפילו הפקר:
notes.en: He is obligated in peret, olelot, forgotten clusters and pe’a: for with all of these “you shall leave” is written, which includes even ownerless property.

notes.he: דלא כתיב ביה תעזוב:
notes.en: And exempt from tithe: since “you shall leave” is not written with it.

messages.text: His obligation to give the gifts to the poor even though the vineyard was at some point ownerless is derived from the repeated phrase: “You shall leave them for the poor.”
@Rav Ashi And now that we have given all of these answers, explaining that Abaye and Rava concede to one another in all the above cases, with regard to what cases do Abaye and Rava disagree?

notes.he: דאיכא דמהני ואיכא דלא מהני ובכולהו מודו אביי ורבא במאי פליגי:
notes.en: And now that we have given all these answers: that there are cases where it is effective and cases where it is not effective, and in all of them Abaye and Rava agree — with regard to what do they disagree?

notes.dh: והשתא דשנינן כל הני שינויי אביי ורבא במאי פליגי
notes.he: וא"ת נימא דפליגי בהכי כגון אדם שנשבע שלא לגרש את אשתו ואחר כך עבר וגירשה דלאביי מהני ולרבא לא מהני גירושין כיון דעבר אמימרא דרחמנא ויש לומר כיון שאין האיסור כמו לא יוכל לשלחה אלא שהוא בדה את האיסור בכה"ג לא אמר רבא דלא מהני וקשיא לרבינו ברוך אמאי לא קאמר דפליגי בהכי כגון אם פדה בכור או מעשר או חרמים לא מהני לכ"ע כדמפרש סוגיא דלאביי לא לקי כיון דלא מהני דהכי אמר אביי לעיל דהיכא דלא מהני לא לקי ולרבא לקי משום דעבר אמימרא דרחמנא צ"ע:
notes.en: And now that we have given all these answers, with regard to what do Abaye and Rava disagree?: And if you say: let us say they disagree in a case like this: a man who swore not to divorce his wife and afterward transgressed and divorced her — for Abaye it is effective, and for Rava the divorce is not effective, since he transgressed the statement of the Merciful One. One can say: since the prohibition is not like “he may not send her away all his days,” but rather he invented the prohibition himself, in such a case Rava did not say that it is not effective. And Rabbeinu Barukh found it difficult: why does it not say that they disagree in this case, for example, where one redeemed a firstborn, or tithe, or dedicated property? It is not effective according to everyone, as the passage explains; so for Abaye he is not flogged, since it is not effective, for so Abaye said above, that where it is not effective, he is not flogged; and for Rava he is flogged, because he transgressed the statement of the Merciful One. This requires further study.

messages.text: They disagree with regard to fixed [ketzutza] interest, and their dispute is like that of Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yoḥanan.
messages.quote: with regard to what cases do Abaye and Rava disagree?

notes.he: [והשתא דשנינן כל הני שינויי אמר לך רבא אמר לך אביי א"כ במאי פליגי פליגי] ברבית קצוצה. (תנא רבית) לאביי דאמר אי עבד מהני לא מהדר (לרבית):
notes.en: [And now that we have given all these answers, “Rava could say to you,” “Abaye could say to you,” with regard to what do they disagree? They disagree] with regard to fixed interest. For Abaye, who said that if one did it, it is effective, he does not return [it].

messages.text: If a debtor paid fixed interest and petitions the court to have it returned to him, since the Torah prohibits the charging of interest, it is repossessed from the creditor by the judges of the court.
6b
If a debtor paid a hint of interest and petitions the court to have it returned to him, it is not repossessed from the creditor by the judges of the court.

notes.he: הבא ע"י מכר כגון המוכר שדהו ואמר אם מעכשיו אתה נותן לי הרי היא לך באלף זוז ואם לגורן בי"ב מנה וברבית קצוצה קמיפלגי אביי דאמר מהני כרבי יוחנן ורבא כר' אלעזר דהכא ליכא קרא לא הכי ולא הכי:
notes.en: A hint of interest [avak ribbit]: that which comes through a sale, for example one who sells his field and says: If you give me [the money] now, it is yours for a thousand zuz, and if at the threshing floor [i.e., later], for twelve maneh [twelve hundred]. And they disagree about fixed interest: Abaye, who says it is effective, [holds] like Rabbi Yoḥanan, and Rava like Rabbi Elazar, for here there is no verse either way.

messages.text: Even fixed interest is not repossessed by the judges.

Abaye holds that transgressions are effective, and the interest now belongs to the creditor and cannot be repossessed, in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan. Therefore, the judges do not appropriate it. Rava holds that transgressions are not effective, and the creditor is in unlawful possession of the interest. Therefore, the judges repossess it, in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Elazar.

notes.he: לרבא דאמר לעולם לא מהני מהדר (לריבית):
notes.en: For Rava, who says it is never effective, he returns [the interest].

messages.text: There, in the dispute concerning fixed interest, do Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yoḥanan disagree with regard to logical reasoning, i.e., the principle of whether transgressions are effective? Not so; rather, they disagree there with regard to the interpretation of the verses,
messages.lead: Rav Aḥa said to Rav Ashi:

notes.he: בתמיה קאמר. התם בקראי פליגי כו':
notes.en: There do they disagree with regard to logical reasoning?: He says it as a question of astonishment. There they disagree with regard to verses etc.

notes.dh: ל"א פליגי ברבית קצוצה וכדרבי אלעזר כו'
notes.he: [א"ל (רב אחא) רבא] לא (התם) [אתי] בקראי (פליגי) [פליגינן] בנשך נתן ותרבית לקח וחי לא יחיה [דמיו בו למיתה ניתן ולא להשבון] היינו טעמא דאביי ורבא דסברי יוצאה בדיינין משום דכתיב קרא [וחי אחיך עמך אל תקח מאתו נשך ותרבית ויראת וחי אחיך עמך] אהדר ליה דרבית דלא תיסב מיניה כי היכי דניחי בהדך:
notes.en: Another version: they disagree with regard to fixed interest, and in line with Rabbi Elazar etc. [He said to him:] No, [there] they disagree about verses: “He has given forth upon interest, and has taken increase; shall he then live? He shall not live” — [his blood is upon him: it was given for death and not for returning]. This is the reason of Abaye and Rava [so the printed text], who hold that it is repossessed by the judges: because the verse is written, [“Take no interest of him or increase, but fear your God, that your brother may live with you”] — return to him the interest, which you should not take from him, so that he may live with you.

messages.text: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Yoḥanan? The verse states: “[He] has given forth upon interest, and has taken increase; shall he then live? He shall not live; he has done all these abominations; he shall be put to death; his blood shall be upon him”. Apparently, a usurer is subject to divine punishment for his life, but the interest is not subject to returning. This is the source for the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan.
messages.quote: Even fixed interest is not repossessed by the judges

verse.he: בַּנֶּשֶׁךְ נָתַן וְתַרְבִּית לָקַח וָחָי לֹא יִחְיֶה אֵת כׇּל־הַתּוֹעֵבוֹת הָאֵלֶּה עָשָׂה מוֹת יוּמָת דָּמָיו בּוֹ יִהְיֶה׃
verse.en: has lent at advance interest, or exacted accrued interest—shall he live? He shall not live! If he has committed any of these abominations, he shall die; he has forfeited his life.

notes.he: כלומר שלא יחיה ולא להשבון ואפי' לרבא מהני דהא כתיב קרא:
notes.en: It was given for life: that is to say, that he shall not live, and not for returning. And even for Rava it is effective, since a verse is written.

messages.text: The source for the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan is from here: “Take no interest of him or increase, but fear your God, that your brother may live with you. You shall not give him your money upon interest, nor give him your provisions for increase; I am the Lord”. In effect, God is saying: I have made a usurer subject to punishment for insufficient fear of Me, but the interest is not subject to returning.

verse.he: אַל־תִּקַּח מֵאִתּוֹ נֶשֶׁךְ וְתַרְבִּית וְיָרֵאתָ מֵאֱלֹהֶיךָ וְחֵי אָחִיךָ עִמָּךְ׃ אֶת־כַּסְפְּךָ לֹא־תִתֵּן לוֹ בְּנֶשֶׁךְ וּבְמַרְבִּית לֹא־תִתֵּן אׇכְלֶךָ׃ אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר־הוֹצֵאתִי אֶתְכֶם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם לָתֵת לָכֶם אֶת־אֶרֶץ כְּנַעַן לִהְיוֹת לָכֶם לֵאלֹהִים׃ {ס}
verse.en: do not exact advance or accrued interest, but fear your God. Let your kin live by your side as such. Do not lend your money at advance interest, nor give your food at accrued interest. I am the ETERNAL your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, to be your God.

messages.text: The source for the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan is from here: “Has lent at advance interest, or exacted accrued interest; shall he live? He shall not live! He has done all these abominations; he shall be put to death; his blood shall be upon him” (Ezekiel 18:13). And an earlier verse states: “If he fathers a son that is a robber, a shedder of blood” (Ezekiel 18:10). Usurers are thereby juxtaposed to shedders of blood, i.e., murderers: Just as the sins of shedders of blood cannot be undone, so too, the sins of usurers cannot be undone.

verse.he: וְהוֹלִיד בֵּן־פָּרִיץ שֹׁפֵךְ דָּם וְעָשָׂה אָח מֵאַחַד מֵאֵלֶּה׃
verse.en: Suppose, now, that he has begotten a son who is a ruffian, a shedder of blood, who does any of these things,

messages.text: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Elazar? As the verse states: “Take no interest of him or increase; but fear your God, that your brother may live with you”. The verse teaches that one must return the interest to the debtor so that he will be able to live together with you.
messages.quote: fixed interest is repossessed by the judges

verse.he: אַל־תִּקַּח מֵאִתּוֹ נֶשֶׁךְ וְתַרְבִּית וְיָרֵאתָ מֵאֱלֹהֶיךָ וְחֵי אָחִיךָ עִמָּךְ׃
verse.en: do not exact advance or accrued interest, but fear your God. Let your kin live by your side as such.

messages.text: But if this matter is not a consequence of the dispute of Abaye and Rava, with regard to what case do Abaye and Rava disagree?

There is perhaps no practical dispute between them, and they disagree only with regard to the theoretical question of whether deviation from what is stated in the Torah is effective. According to the opinion of Abaye, if there is no verse teaching otherwise, a transgression is presumed to be effective. According to the opinion of Rava, it is presumed to be not effective. They, therefore, disagree as to which halakhot reflect the rule and which are exceptions.

notes.he: דאביי סבר שינוי ששינה ועבר על דעת המקום קונה בר מהיכא דכתיבי קראי ולרבא לא קני אלא היכא דכתיבי קראי. ולא איתפרש לן דליהוי מידי בינייהו אלא תירוצי דהני תיובתא דמר אית ליה דמשום דמהני ולא מהני הוא ומר אית ליה משום טעמא דקראי. ונ"ב דמצינו למימר בשינוי קונה כגון גוזל עצים ועשאן כלים צמר ועשאן בגדים דלאביי קנה ואינו משלם אלא עצים וצמר ולרבא לא קנה ומשלם הבגדים והכלים וכי פרכינן לעיל לרבא מהא דקתני הגוזל עצים ועשאן כלים כו' לא תימא שאני התם דכתיב אשר גזל אלא הכי תימא אנא דאמרי כמאן דאמר שינוי לא קני דפלוגתא היא בבבא קמא בפרק מרובה (בבא קמא דף סו.) ובהגוזל קמא (שם צד.) דאיכא למאן דאמר שינוי קונה ומפיק טעמא מאשר גזל כעין שגזל ואיכא למאן דאמר שינוי לא קני ויליף מוהשיב את הגזילה מכל מקום אם כן מה ת"ל אשר גזל לומר שאינו מוסיף חומש על גזל אביו:
notes.en: With regard to whether a change acquires [Rashi’s text reads shinui koneh, “a change acquires”; the Davidson renders it “whether deviation is effective”]: for Abaye holds that a change by which one changed and transgressed the will of the Omnipresent acquires, except where verses are written; and for Rava it does not acquire, except where verses are written. And it is not explained to us that there is any [practical difference] between them, only the answers to these refutations: one Sage holds that it is because it is effective or not effective, and the other Sage holds that it is because of the reasoning of the verses. [A further remark, marked נ״ב:] We could say [that they differ] with regard to whether a change acquires, for example one who robbed wood and made it into vessels, or wool and made it into garments: for Abaye he acquired them and pays only for wood and wool, and for Rava he did not acquire them and pays the garments and the vessels. And when we challenged Rava above from what is taught, “One who robs wood and fashions it into vessels etc.,” [he would] not say “it is different there, as it is written ‘that he took by robbery’”; rather, he would say: I hold like the one who says a change does not acquire. For this is a dispute in Bava Kamma, chapter Merubba (Bava Kamma 66a) and in the first [chapter] HaGozel (ibid. 94a): there is one who says a change acquires and derives the reason from “that he took by robbery,” like what he robbed; and there is one who says a change does not acquire and derives it from “and he shall restore the stolen item,” in any case. If so, why does the verse state “that he took by robbery”? To say that he does not add a fifth for his father’s robbery.

notes.he: ובין האי לישנא ללישנא דשמיע לי בשינוי קונה ליכא מידי אלא זה ירושלמי וזה בבלי:
notes.en: This is the reading we have: “Another version: with regard to these answers that we answered.” And between this version and the version I heard, “with regard to whether a change acquires,” there is no difference, except that one is a “Jerusalem” [reading] and the other a “Babylonian” one.

notes.he: בשינוי קונה כדאמרן:
notes.en: [Rather, with regard to what] do they disagree? With regard to whether a change acquires, as we said.

messages.text: In accordance with the answers we answered above, Abaye and Rava disagree with regard to fixed interest. According to the opinion of Abaye that transgressions are effective, the creditor does not need to return the interest, as he has acquired it. But according to the opinion of Rava that transgressions are not effective, the creditor must return the interest, as it still belongs to the debtor.
messages.lead: § The Gemara presents an alternative version of the answer:

messages.text: But Abaye also holds that we repossess fixed interest by the authority of the judges,

In the event that this one, who was collecting a debt from another, demanded that he pay four dinars as interest, and the debtor gave to the creditor, in his store, a cloak that was worth five dinars in place of the four dinars of interest, the halakha is that when we repossess the interest from the creditor, we repossess only four dinars from him. And as for that additional one dinar, one presumes the debtor gave it to him as a gift.

notes.he: האי מאן דמסיק בחבריה זוזי וכבר עלה הריבית שחייב לו ליתן ד' זוזי דרביתא (וסגי) ויהיב [ליה] לוה למלוה [בגויהו]:
notes.en: This one who was owed money by another, and the interest had already risen, so that he owed him four zuz of interest, and the borrower gave the lender [in their place] …

messages.text: We repossess all five dinars from him. What is the reason? All of it came into his possession by virtue of a payment of interest.
messages.quote: we repossess only four dinars from him

messages.text: In any event, it is clear that Abaye holds that fixed interest is repossessed by the court.
The printed Aramaic marks “in his store” (beḥanuteih) for correction to “in their place” (begavayhu), the reading Rabbeinu Gershom has.

Rather, there may be no practical dispute between them, as when Abaye and Rava disagree, it is only with regard to the theoretical question of whether deviation from what is stated in the Torah is effective.

notes.dh: גלימא דשויא חמשה בארבעה כי מפקינן כו' אלמא אביי סבר דמפקינן מיניה
notes.he: אלא אביי ורבא קא מפלגי בשנוי קונה היינו שנוי קונה דעבר אמימרא דרחמנ' דשינה [בציוויו] לאביי קונה היינו מהני לרבא לא. ל"א קא מיפלגי (בהני שינוי) [הני בשינוי] דשנינן [דאמרן] דאביי אמר מהני ומתרץ לטעמיה [ורבא אמר לא מהני ומתרץ לטעמיה] היינו (שינוי) נמי קונה דקאמר אלא דבהאי לישנא מפרש [טפי]:
notes.en: A cloak worth five for four: when we repossess etc. Evidently Abaye holds that we repossess it from him. Rather, Abaye and Rava disagree with regard to whether a change acquires: that is, a change by which one transgressed the statement of the Merciful One, deviating from His command — for Abaye it acquires, that is, it is effective; for Rava it does not. Another version: they disagree [about these answers with regard to change] that we gave, that Abaye says it is effective and answers according to his reasoning, [and Rava says it is not effective and answers according to his reasoning]. This too is the “acquires” it speaks of, only that this version explains it [more fully].

messages.text: § Returning to the topic of blemished animals, the Sages taught in a baraita:

Why must the verse state: “But whatever has a blemish, you shall not offer; for it shall not be acceptable for you”? If it serves to teach that you may not slaughter a blemished animal as a sacrifice even if it has been consecrated, that is already stated below, later on in the passage, as the Gemara will soon explain. Rather, why must the verse state that you may not offer a blemished animal? This serves to teach that you may not consecrate it.

verse.he: כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־בּוֹ מוּם לֹא תַקְרִיבוּ כִּי־לֹא לְרָצוֹן יִהְיֶה לָכֶם׃
verse.en: You shall not offer any that has a defect, for it will not be accepted in your favor.

notes.dh: תנו רבנן אם בל תשחטו הרי כבר אמור למטה
notes.he: שלא ישחטו בעל מום למזבח. ולקמן מפרש לה והקטרה נמי וזריקת דמו לקמן מפרש:
notes.en: The Sages taught: If [it is for] “you may not slaughter,” that is already stated below: that one may not slaughter a blemished animal for the altar; and further on it explains it. And burning too, and sprinkling its blood, are explained further on.

notes.he: א"כ מה ת"ל לא תקריבו לא תקדישו:
notes.en: If so, why does the verse state “you shall not offer”? [To teach:] you shall not consecrate.

notes.he: (ת"ל כל) [מום עובר מנין] (דיכול) [מדיכול] למימר אשר בו מום לא לרצון יהיה וכתב כל לרבות בעל מום עובר:
notes.en: [From where do we derive a transient blemish?] Since it could have said, “that which has a blemish… shall not be acceptable,” and it wrote “whatever [kol],” to include an animal with a transient blemish.

notes.he: נמי לא צריך (ואי) [דאי] משום בל תשחטו בעל מום אתא והרי כבר נאמר למטה כדמפרש לקמן דשחיטת בעל מום מקרא אחרינא נפקא:
notes.en: “You shall not offer” is also not needed [for this], for if it comes for the prohibition against slaughtering a blemished animal, that is already stated below, as is explained further on, that slaughtering a blemished animal is derived from another verse.

notes.he: דהאי לא תקריבו מוקים ליה לקמן דהיינו לא תקדישו]:
notes.en: [For the prohibition against consecrating: for this “you shall not offer” is interpreted further on as “you shall not consecrate.”]

messages.text: One who consecrates blemished animals for sacrifice on the altar violates five separate categories of prohibition.

notes.he: לקמן יליף להו:
notes.en: Five categories: further on it derives them.

notes.he: והקטירן כולן לעולה:
notes.en: One who consecrates blemished animals: and burned them all as a burnt offering.

messages.text: He is liable for violating the prohibitions: You may not offer a blemished animal as an offering, i.e., you may not consecrate it; you may not slaughter it; and for the prohibition: You may not sprinkle its blood; and for the prohibition: You may not burn all of it on the altar; and for the prohibition: You may not burn part of it.

notes.dh: ועל הקטרת כולו ועל הקטרת מקצת
notes.he: בין אם מקטירו כולו בין אם מקטירו מקצתו עובר משום בל תקטירו:
notes.en: And for burning all of it and for burning part of it: whether he burns all of it or burns part of it, he transgresses the prohibition “you shall not burn.”

messages.text: One also violates a prohibition against the collection of the blood.

The Master said above: If one suggests that the prohibition in Leviticus 22:20 teaches that you may not slaughter a blemished animal as an offering, that is already stated below, later on in the passage. Where is it stated? As it is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: you may not slaughter … that is already stated below

messages.text: Why must the verse state: “Blind, or broken, or maimed, or having a cyst, or scabbed, or scurvy, you shall not offer”? If this serves to teach that you may not consecrate them, that is already stated above, in verse 20. Rather, why must the verse state that you may not offer these animals? This serves to teach that you may not slaughter them if they have been consecrated.

verse.he: עַוֶּרֶת אוֹ שָׁבוּר אוֹ־חָרוּץ אוֹ־יַבֶּלֶת אוֹ גָרָב אוֹ יַלֶּפֶת לֹא־תַקְרִיבוּ אֵלֶּה לַיהֹוָה וְאִשֶּׁה לֹא־תִתְּנוּ מֵהֶם עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: Anything blind, or injured, or maimed, or with a wen, boil-scar, or scurvy—such you shall not offer to GOD; you shall not put any of them on the altar as offerings by fire to GOD.

notes.he: אם בל תקדיש הרי כבר אמור למעל' כדאמרן דהאי כל אשר בו מום לא תקריבו היינו לא תקדישו:
notes.en: If [it is for] the prohibition against consecrating, that is already stated above, as we said, that this “whatever has a blemish you shall not offer” means “you shall not consecrate.”

messages.text: The verse states: “Nor make an offering by fire of them upon the altar unto the Lord”. These words teach that one may not burn a blemished animal in the fires of the altar. I have derived only that it is prohibited to burn all of the animal. From where is it derived that it is prohibited to burn some portions of the animal? The verse states: “Of them,” which prohibits the burning of even part of them.

notes.he: הקטרת אימורין:
notes.en: These are fires: the burning of the sacrificial portions.

notes.he: היינו בל תקטירו:
notes.en: “Offering by fire [isheh]”: these are the fires, that is, the prohibition against burning.

messages.text: From where is it derived that sprinkling the blood of a blemished animal is prohibited? The verse states: “Upon the altar,” thereby indicating that one may not sacrifice any part of it, even its blood, on the altar. The verse continues: “Unto the Lord,” which serves to include the scapegoat of Yom Kippur in this prohibition, that it may not be blemished even though it is not sacrificed on the altar.

notes.he: שהמקדישו בעל מום לוקה משום לא תקדישו:
notes.en: To include the scapegoat: that one who consecrates it blemished is flogged on account of “you shall not consecrate.”

notes.he: [לבעל מום שלא [יביא] בעל מום] אע"ג דאינו בא לה' [הא] אין הגורל קובע אלא בראוי לשם כלומר דאפילו שעיר המשתלח בעינן (הכא) [תם]:
notes.en: “Unto the Lord,” to include the scapegoat: [with regard to a blemished animal, that one may not bring a blemished one,] even though it does not go to the Lord. [But] the lottery establishes only what is fit for the Name; that is to say, even for the scapegoat we require [an unblemished animal].

messages.caption: One who consecrates a blemished animal for the altar and offers it: the five prohibitions and the words they come from.

messages.text: And does the term: “Unto the Lord,” serve to include the scapegoat? But isn’t it taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: “Unto the Lord,” which serves to include the scapegoat

messages.text: The Torah condemns one who slaughters an offering outside the Temple “and has not brought it unto the door of the Tent of Meeting, to present it as an offering unto the Lord”. If the verse had stated only “offering,” I would derive that one is liable even for slaughtering animals consecrated for Temple maintenance outside the Temple, for they are also called an offering, as it is stated: “And we have brought the Lord’s offering, what every man has found: Articles of gold” (Numbers 31:50).

verse.he: וְאֶל־פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד לֹא הֱבִיאוֹ לְהַקְרִיב קׇרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה לִפְנֵי מִשְׁכַּן יְהֹוָה דָּם יֵחָשֵׁב לָאִישׁ הַהוּא דָּם שָׁפָךְ וְנִכְרַת הָאִישׁ הַהוּא מִקֶּרֶב עַמּוֹ׃
verse.en: and does not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to present it as an offering to GOD, before GOD’s Tabernacle: bloodguilt shall be imputed to them; having shed blood, that person shall be cut off from among their people.

notes.he: בשחוטי חוץ כתיב ואל פתח אהל מועד לא הביאו וגו' להקריב קרבן לה':
notes.en: “Offering”: written with regard to slaughtering outside: “and has not brought it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting… to present it as an offering unto the Lord.”

notes.dh: הכי גרסינן אי קרבן שומע אני כו'
notes.he: ומהדר אדלעיל בתורת כהנים דקתני לעיל יכול השוחט חולין בפנים יהא חייב ת"ל קרבן על הקרבן הוא חייב ואינו חייב על החולין אי קרבן שומע אני כו' כלומר אי קרבן קא דרשת שומע אני אפילו השוחט בדק הבית בחוץ יהא חייב כרת שהרי הם נקראו קרבן כענין שנאמר ונקרב את קרבן ה' וגו' כלי זהב אצעדה וצמיד דהיינו למלאכת המשכן:
notes.en: This is the reading: “If ‘offering,’ I would derive etc.”: it refers back to what is above in Torat Kohanim, which teaches above: One might think that one who slaughters non-sacred animals inside [the Temple] is liable; the verse states “offering”: for an offering he is liable, and he is not liable for non-sacred animals. “If ‘offering,’ I would derive etc.,” that is to say: if you expound “offering,” I would derive that even one who slaughters [animals consecrated for] Temple maintenance outside is liable to karet, for they are called an offering, as it is stated: “And we have brought the Lord’s offering etc.: articles of gold, armlets and bracelets,” which were for the work of the Tabernacle.

notes.he: [והתניא קרבן האי דכתיב ואל פתח אהל מועד לא הביאו להקריב קרבן (מעט) [שומע אני] אף קדשי בדק הבית שנקראו קרבן אם שחטו בחוץ יהא חייב:
notes.en: [But isn’t it taught: “offering”: this that is written, “and has not brought it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, to present it as an offering” — I would understand that even items consecrated for Temple maintenance, which are called an offering, if one slaughtered them outside, he would be liable.

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states: “And has not brought it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting”. This teaches that one is liable only for sacrificing an animal fit to be sacrificed within the entrance of the Tent of Meeting or the Temple due to the prohibition of slaughtering offerings outside the Temple. But one is not liable for sacrificing an animal not fit to be sacrificed within the entrance of the Tent of Meeting due to the prohibition of slaughtering offerings outside the Temple.

notes.he: כגון קדשי בדק הבית שאינם ראויין לבא לפתח אהל מועד שהרי בעלי מומין הן דאמרן לעיל המתפיס תמימין לבדק הבית עובר בלא תעשה:
notes.en: That is not fit for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting: such as items consecrated for Temple maintenance, which are not fit to come to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, since they are blemished animals, as we said above: one who assigns unblemished animals to Temple maintenance transgresses a prohibition.

messages.text: I might exclude these animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, but not exclude the red heifer of purification, whose ashes are used to purge the impurity imparted by a corpse, and the scapegoat, despite the fact that neither are sacrificed on the altar, as they are unblemished and therefore fit to come to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Therefore, the verse states: “Unto the Lord,” to teach that one is liable only for those animals that are exclusively the Lord’s as offerings. These, the red heifer of purification and the scapegoat, are excluded, as they are not exclusively the Lord’s as offerings, but rather they serve unique ritual functions.

notes.dh: אוציא את אלו ולא אוציא את פרת חטאת
notes.he: פרה אדומה שאם שחטה בחוץ שלא כמצוותה שלא ע"ג מערכתה שיתחייב כרת וכן שעיר המשתלח אם שחטו בחוץ יתחייב כרת שהרי תמימין הן דבפרה כתיב (במדבר י״ט:ב׳) אשר אין בה מום ושעיר מרבינן (ליה) לעיל שלא יהא בו מום:
notes.en: I exclude these, but not the red heifer of purification: the red heifer, that if he slaughtered it outside, not in its prescribed manner, not on its pyre, he would be liable to karet; and likewise the scapegoat, if he slaughtered it outside he would be liable to karet, since they are unblemished: for with the heifer it is written (Numbers 19:2), “in which there is no blemish,” and the scapegoat we include above, that it may not have a blemish.

notes.he: אלמא להוציא שעיר הוא:
notes.en: These are excluded: evidently it is to exclude the scapegoat.

notes.dh: ולא אוציא פרת חטאת ושעיר המשתלח
notes.he: פירש"י ביומא פ' שני שעירי (יומא דף סג:) דל"ג פרת חטאת שהרי בפ' בתרא דזבחים (דף קיב.) תנן פרת חטאת ששרפה חוץ מגיתה ושעיר המשתלח שהקריבו בחוץ פטור שנאמר ואל פתח אהל מועד לא הביאו כל שאינו ראוי לפתח אהל מועד ופריך בגמ' עלה ושעיר המשתלח לא ראוי לפתח אהל מועד הוא והתניא ומייתי הך ברייתא דהכא ואי גרס בה פרת חטאת כי היכי דפריך משעיר המשתלח הכי נמי הוה מצי למיפרך מפרת חטאת ואין התירוץ שייך אפרת חטאת ומשום הכי פרש"י דל"ג ליה וקשה על הא דמשני עלה בזבחים (דף קיג:) לא קשיא כאן קודם הגרלה כאן לאחר הגרלה קודם הגרלה הוה ראוי לפתח אהל מועד ואפילו הכי ממעט ליה קרא דאם הקריבו בחוץ פטור והא תניא בהדיא ביומא (דף סב:) דקודם הגרלה חייב השוחטו בחוץ וי"ל דלפי המסקנא דזבחים (שם) ניחא דמסיק לא קשיא כאן קודם ודוי כאן לאחר ודוי ולפי זה אפשר תרווייהו לאחר הגרלה אבל קודם הגרלה אפשר דחייב השוחט בחוץ כי ההיא דיומא:
notes.en: In brief: Rashi in Yoma, chapter Shenei Se’irei (Yoma 63b), says the words “red heifer of purification” should not be read in this baraita. The mishna in the last chapter of Zevaḥim (112a) exempts one who burns the red heifer outside its pit or sacrifices the scapegoat outside, “as it is stated: ‘and has not brought it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting’ — whatever is not fit for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,” and the Gemara there challenges only from the scapegoat, citing this baraita. Had the baraita named the red heifer, the Gemara could have challenged from the heifer as well, and the answer given there does not fit the heifer. Tosafot then ask about the answer in Zevaḥim, “Here before the lottery, here after the lottery”: it implies that before the lottery, when the scapegoat is fit for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, the verse still exempts one who sacrifices it outside, yet a baraita in Yoma (62b) says explicitly that before the lottery one who slaughters it outside is liable. They answer that by the conclusion in Zevaḥim, “Here before the confession, here after the confession,” both cases may be after the lottery, while before the lottery one may indeed be liable for slaughtering it outside, as in Yoma. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: אוציא את אלו קדשי בדק הבית דהיינו נמי בעלי מומין כדאמרינן לקמן דאין מקדישין לבדק הבית אלא בעלי מומין ולא אוציא פרת חטאת ושעיר המשתלח שהן תמימין וראויין הן לפתח אהל מועד]:
notes.en: I exclude these: items consecrated for Temple maintenance, which are also blemished animals, as we say further on that one consecrates for Temple maintenance only blemished animals; but I do not exclude the red heifer of purification and the scapegoat, which are unblemished and fit for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.]

messages.text: In any event, the term “unto the Lord” is interpreted as excluding, rather than including, the scapegoat.

There, in the baraita discussing offerings slaughtered outside the Temple, the halakha is derived from the context of the verse. The verse states: “And has not brought it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting”, which serves to include any unblemished animal. Therefore, the following term: “Unto the Lord,” serves to exclude certain exceptions to the rule. Here, where the verse states “fire” (Leviticus 22:22), which serves to exclude animals not burned on the altar from the prohibition, the term: “Unto the Lord,” serves to include exceptions to that principle.

notes.he: דאל פתח אהל מועד מרבה כל התמימין הקדושין להתחייב עליהן בחוץ לה' תו למה לי ודאי להוציא הוא:
notes.en: There: where “to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting” includes all consecrated unblemished animals, to make one liable for them outside, why do I need “unto the Lord” further? It is certainly to exclude.

notes.he: גבי בעלי מומין כתיב (שם כב) ואשה לא תתנו מהם וגו' ומשמע העולה לאישים חייב עליו מקדישו בעל מום משום לא תקדישו אבל שאינו עולה לאשים לא ואימעיט ליה שעיר הילכך לה' להוציא למה לי הא מיעטיה מואשה אלא ודאי לרבות הוא:
notes.en: But here, where “fire” is to exclude: with regard to blemished animals it is written (Leviticus 22), “nor make an offering by fire of them etc.,” which implies: for what goes up to the fires, one who consecrates it blemished is liable on account of “you shall not consecrate,” but what does not go up to the fires, not; and the scapegoat is excluded. Therefore, why do I need “unto the Lord” to exclude, when it was already excluded by “fire”? Rather, it is certainly to include.

notes.he: להקרבה חייב משום שחוטי חוץ יצאו אלו פרת חטאת ושעיר המשתלח שאין מיוחדין להקרבה אלמא לה' להוציא הוא. לה' למה לי ש"מ מאי אשים (דקאמר מדבר דמרבינן באשים) [דקא מרבי דמרצין כאשים] לשם אסור בבעל מום. ושעיר המשתלח נמי מרצה [הוא] לעזאזל כאשים לשם הלכך בעינן תם:
notes.en: The verse states “unto the Lord”: those that are exclusively the Lord’s, for sacrifice — for them one is liable on account of slaughtering outside. These are excluded, the red heifer of purification and the scapegoat, which are not exclusively for sacrifice. Evidently “unto the Lord” is to exclude. [Here,] why do I need “unto the Lord”? Learn from it: what is “fire”? [What it includes is whatever effects atonement like the fires] to the Name: it is forbidden with a blemish. And the scapegoat too effects atonement, to Azazel, like the fires to the Name; therefore we require an unblemished animal.

messages.text: The baraita indicates that the reason why a blemished animal may not be brought as the scapegoat is that the verse writes: “Unto the Lord.” One may infer that had the verse not included the scapegoat by employing the term: “Unto the Lord,” I would say that it is permitted to sacrifice a blemished scapegoat.

notes.he: לאקדושיה:
notes.en: It is permitted: to consecrate it.

messages.text: Now, of the two goats of the Yom Kippur service, one is selected as the scapegoat and one as an offering by lottery. As a rule, the lottery can establish the animals in their respective roles only if each is fit for either role. Given that a blemished animal cannot be sacrificed as an offering, it cannot be designated as the scapegoat either. The term “unto the Lord” therefore seems unnecessary.

notes.he: של שם קובע אלא בדבר הראוי לשם דכי מייתי ומגריל לא ידע אהי מינייהו סליק גורל של שם הלכך בעל כרחיך תרוייהו בעינן תמימין וקרא למה לי:
notes.en: But the lottery: of [the goat for] the Name establishes only what is fit for the Name, for when he brings [the goats] and holds the lottery, he does not know on which of them the lot for the Name will come up. Therefore, perforce, we require both to be unblemished; so why do I need the verse?

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this baraita? It is in accordance with the opinion of Ḥanan the Egyptian, who said:
messages.quote: had the verse not included the scapegoat

notes.he: ואיצטריך לה' לרבות חנן המצרי היא דאמר אפילו דם בכוס [של שעיר של שם שעדיין לא נזרק ונאבד שעיר המשתלח או שהומם מביא חברו אחר לשעיר המשתלח]:
notes.en: Rav Yosef said: Whose is this [baraita], for which “unto the Lord” was needed to include? It is Ḥanan the Egyptian, who said: even [if the blood of the goat for the Name] is in the cup [and has not yet been sprinkled, and the scapegoat was lost or became blemished, he brings another as a partner, as the scapegoat].

messages.text: If the scapegoat dies before being sent to the wilderness, even if the other goat has already been slaughtered and its blood collected in the cup, the slaughtered goat is nevertheless a fit offering, and the priest brings another goat and pairs it with the slaughtered goat to serve as the scapegoat.
This new scapegoat is thereby designated without a lottery, and one might therefore suppose it can be blemished. The term “unto the Lord” is therefore needed to teach that it must be unblemished.

notes.he: להאי שעיר שנשחט כלומר דשלא בהגרלה מביאו דהא לא מצי למיגרל שכבר נשחט חבירו וכי היכי דמצי מייתי שלא בהגרלה אליבא דחנן וסד"א דהכי נמי מצי מייתי ליה בעל מום להכי איצטריך ליה:
notes.en: And pairs it: with this goat that was slaughtered; that is to say, he brings it without a lottery, since he cannot hold a lottery, as its fellow has already been slaughtered. And just as he can bring it without a lottery according to Ḥanan, one might think he can also bring a blemished one; that is why it was needed.

messages.text: Granted that you learn from the statement of Ḥanan the Egyptian that he holds that there is no deferral of the second goat once it has already been slaughtered. But do you learn from him that the new scapegoat need not be designated by a lottery? Perhaps the priest brings two potential scapegoats and performs a lottery to decide between them. Therefore, the question again arises: What need is there for the term “unto the Lord”?
messages.quote: brings another goat and pairs it with the slaughtered goat

notes.he: ואכתי אמאי איצטריך (לה') [לחנן]:
notes.en: And still, why is it needed [according to Ḥanan]?

notes.he: נהי דשמעת ליה לחנן:
notes.en: Granted that you heard Ḥanan:

notes.he: [דאמר אפילו דם בכוס מביא ומזווג לו להכי קאמר לאשמועינן דלא הוי דחוי דנשחט כל זמן שלא נזרק ודמו יש לו תקנה אע"פ שמת חבירו או נאבד דמביא אחר ומזווג לו אבל שלא בהגרלה מי שמעת ליה דמביאו דלמא מייתי ומגריל קאמר וכיצד עושה יביא שנים ויגריל עליהם ואותו שיבא גורלו לשם יניחו ואותו שיבוא גורלו לעזאזל יביאו ומזווגו לזה ראשון שדמו בכוס וכיון דמצרכן הגרלה מצריכו נמי להיות תם שאין הגורל קובע אלא בראוי לשם]:
notes.en: [Who said: even if the blood is in the cup, he brings another and pairs it with it. He says this to teach us that it is not deferred: the slaughtered one, so long as its blood has not been sprinkled, has a remedy even though its fellow died or was lost, and he brings another and pairs it with it. But that he brings it without a lottery — did you hear that from him? Perhaps he means he brings and holds a lottery. And how does he do it? He brings two and holds a lottery over them; the one whose lot comes up for the Name he sets aside, and the one whose lot comes up for Azazel he brings and pairs with the first one, whose blood is in the cup. And since he requires a lottery for them, he also requires it to be unblemished, since the lottery establishes only what is fit for the Name.]

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this baraita? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, as it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: דאיצטריך לה' לרבות ר' שמעון היא דאמר יביא חבירו שלא בהגרלה דמהו דתימא כי היכי דלא בעי הגרלה תו לא ליבעי נמי תם קמ"ל:
notes.en: Whose is this, for which “unto the Lord” was needed to include? It is Rabbi Shimon, who said he brings its fellow without a lottery. One might think: just as it does not require a lottery, so too it should not require an unblemished animal. It teaches us.

messages.text: If one of the two goats dies, the priest brings another goat without another lottery; this is the statement of Rabbi Shimon.
It is this scapegoat that, absent the term “unto the Lord,” could have been blemished.

notes.he: ואמאי ליסליק אדעתין דלא בעי תם נהי דלא בעינן הגרלה לחברו לזה שמביא עכשו כיון דהא אגריל עליה מעיקרא. על אותו שמת ועל אותו של שם אלא משום דלא בעינן גופי דשני (דאחזי להגרלה אטו אותו) [ראוי אותו שנשאר דאי מצרכת ליה להאי שמביא הגרלה הוי] משמע הגרלה קמייתא בטילה ומיפסל גופיה דההוא דקאי דלא מת הלכך [לא] צריך תו הגרלה הא לאו הכי הוה סבר ר' שמעון דבעי הגרלה. וכיון דבעי הגרלה לא מייתי בעל מום [דכיון] דצריך הגרלה בעי למיהוי תם:
notes.en: [The printed edition’s note: It seems that our Rabbi read in the Gemara: “Granted that you heard Rabbi Shimon say that it does not require a lottery, etc. Rather, Rava said, etc.,” and on this our Rabbi explained “and why would it occur to us, etc.”; and see Rashi here, who also cites this reading and rejects it.] And why would it occur to us that it does not require an unblemished animal? Granted that we do not require a lottery for the fellow that he brings now, since he already held a lottery over it at the outset, over the one that died and the one for the Name — but rather it is because [the printed note suggests: so as not to disqualify the second one, the one still standing] we require the second one [to remain fit]: for if you require a lottery for the one he brings, that implies the first lottery is void, and the one still standing, which did not die, would be disqualified. Therefore [no] further lottery is required; otherwise, Rabbi Shimon would have held that a lottery is required. And since a lottery would be required, he does not bring a blemished one, [for] whatever requires a lottery must be unblemished. [The Hebrew here is uncertain; this follows the printed corrections.]

messages.text: No, the term in the verse is necessary for a case where the scapegoat became blemished on that day of Yom Kippur, after it had been designated, and then the priest desacralized it by transferring its sanctity onto another blemished goat.

notes.he: לאחר הגרלה וחיללו על חבירו והוא בעל מום נמי וקמ"ל דהאי שחיללו לקי משום דהקדיש בעל מום ולהכי נקט חיללו דאי לאו דחיללו על בעל מום ליכא מלקות דלא תקדישו על השני:
notes.en: Such as where it became blemished: after the lottery, and he desacralized it onto its fellow, which is also blemished. And it teaches us that the one who desacralized it is flogged because he consecrated a blemished animal. And that is why it speaks of desacralizing: for if he had not desacralized it onto a blemished animal, there would be no lashes for “you shall not consecrate” on the second.

notes.dh: וקרא למה לי כגון שהומם לאחר הגרלה וחיללו על חבירו
notes.he: והוא נמי בעל מום וקמ"ל דהאי שחיללו לקי משום דהקדישו בעל מום ולהכי נקט חיללו דאי לאו דחיללו על בעל מום ליכא מלקות דלא תקדישו על השני:
notes.en: Why do I need the verse? Such as where it became blemished after the lottery and he desacralized it onto its fellow: and that one too is blemished. And it teaches us that the one who desacralized it is flogged, because he consecrated it blemished. And that is why it speaks of desacralizing: for if he had not desacralized it onto a blemished one, there would be no lashes for “you shall not consecrate” on the second.

notes.he: אמר רבא לא נצרכה לכתוב לה' אלא (כגון) שהומם שעיר המשתלח מאחר שהוגרל וחללו על שעיר אחר בעל מום בשלמא מעיקרא קודם שהוגרלו בעינן שיהיו שניהם תמימין דלא ידעינן איזה מיקבע לשם אבל הכא כשהומם מאחר שהוגרל דהא מינכר ההוא דשם דתם הוא אימא לא לקי כי מייתי אידך בעל מום קמ"ל. ל"א טעמא דכתיב קרא לה' כו':
notes.en: Rava said: it was necessary to write “unto the Lord” only for where the scapegoat became blemished after it was selected by lottery, and he desacralized it onto another goat that is blemished. Granted, initially, before they were selected by lottery, we require that both be unblemished, since we do not know which will be designated for the Name. But here, when it became blemished after the lottery, since the one for the Name is recognizable as unblemished, I would say he is not flogged when he brings the other, blemished one. It teaches us. Another version: the reason is that the verse wrote “unto the Lord” etc.

notes.he: להכי איצטריך כגון שהומם שעיר המשתלח לאחר שהוגרל וחיללו על אחר כו'. אלא אמר רבינא איצטרי' לה' לרבות ולאו להכי אתא כדקאמרת לרבות שעיר המשתלח לבעל מום אלא להכי אתא לרבות לשעיר המשתלח למחוסר זמן והכא במאי עסקינן שהיה לו חולה מסוכן בתוך ביתו לאותו שמכר שעיר המשתלח ושחטה לאמו של שעיר המשתלח ביו"כ לצורך החולה סד"א בנה שהוא לצורך עזאזל לאו [בר] שחיטה הוא ולא ליתסר מיתתו בעזאזל משום [איסור] אותו ואת בנו לא תשחטו ביום אחד קמ"ל לה' לרבות דאסור דאמרי במערבא דחייתו לצוק זו היא שחיטתו ואסור:
notes.en: Rather, Rava said: it was needed for this, for example where the scapegoat became blemished after it was selected by lottery and he desacralized it onto another, etc. Rather, Ravina said: “unto the Lord” was needed to include, and it does not come for this, as you said, to include the scapegoat with regard to a blemished animal; rather, it comes to include the scapegoat with regard to [an animal] lacking in time. And with what are we dealing here? Where the one who sold the scapegoat had a dangerously ill person in his house, and he slaughtered the scapegoat’s mother on Yom Kippur for the needs of the sick person. One might think that its offspring, which is for Azazel, is not subject to slaughter, and so its death at Azazel should not be forbidden on account of the prohibition “it and its young you shall not slaughter in one day.” “Unto the Lord” teaches us to include it, that it is forbidden, for they say in the West [the Land of Israel]: pushing it off the cliff is its slaughter, and it is forbidden. [The printed edition’s note: up to here belongs to the previous page.]

messages.text: Rava’s explanation continues on 7a, where the Gemara spells out why this case needs a verse.
